LESSON: LENGTH

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.1: Length
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Length, part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can the length of a chalkboard be measured using a metre stick?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. measure length in metres,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Length in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. add length in metres,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Length in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. subtract length in metres,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Length in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. estimate length up to 10 metres,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Length in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate measuring length in metres in real life situations. ● In purposive pairs/ groups, learners are guided to use metre sticks to measure various distances using appropriate Assistive technology for movement with physical support and record their results by writing/ stamping/ mounting/ typing on adapted digital devices using appropriate Assistive technology and physical support. ● Learners are appropriately positioned/ seated on devices whose worktops are at a suitable height and guided in purposive pairs/ groups to prepare 5 metres long strings with knots at intervals of one 1. support to measure long distances. ● In purposive pairs/ groups, learners are guided to measure the lengths of the 4 walls in their classroom using any alternative functional part of the body and/ appropriate Assistive technology for movement and manipulation and add the lengths which they record by writing/ typing/ mounting/ stamping with physical support. ● In purposive pairs/ groups, SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Length together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: learner uses digital devices to record videos of classmates measuring length.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: learner works out questions involving addition of length in real life situations

Values:
Unity: learner appreciates peers’ effort as they measure the lengths of various objects in and around the classroom.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Self-efficacy: learner estimates distances around the school compound up to 10 metres, measure the actual distances and

compare results.

• Social cohesion: learner works harmoniously with peers to estimate distances around the school compound.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate skills used in preparing 5 metres long strings with knots at intervals of one metre to weaving

skills in Creative Activities.
